owner: minimal_loop after-tool completion of a direct prompt that created a missing path
capture: fixtures/recorded/runs.jsonl is a hand-reduced excerpt of three CommandAgent runs of the L-152 generic bench (off arm, binary built from b2c3b372, the base of Issue #921), observed before the fix. Each line names its run_dir (bench root replaced by <bench>), the events.jsonl path inside it, the SHA-256 of that events file, the step_obligation_scope fields (session_scope, step_kind, effective_required_paths, initially_missing_paths, completion_contract_paths), the number of provider requests, and the events rows from the step_obligation_scope row to the loop_stop (provider_request, tool_call_raw, tool_execute, loop_stop; provider_response, provider_turn_duration, and runtime_bash_policy rows omitted), each with its line number in that events file. Only the event name, tool name, tool status, stop reason, and Bash command are kept; workspace paths are replaced by <p1>/<p2>, and the request text, task material, provider, model, and timings are left out. The shapes are the three named in the issue: a first Write that ends the run (events.jsonl:9-11), ls -F then Read then Write (events.jsonl:9-22), and a Bash touch alone (events.jsonl:9-12). Nothing is added that the records do not hold: none of them has a Bash run of the written file or a final answer after the stop. Sessions: per the S-152a investigation the completed write-only and ls-read-write runs (the 31 unexecuted completions) have saved sessions ending at the last tool result (session_saved=true); the touch-only run is outside those 31 and its session was not checked (session_saved=null). Runs that failed with an error (the 28 correct-but-stagnated runs of the same investigation) have no saved session, because the direct action saves the session only after the run returns Ok; no session content is reconstructed here.
